fluff.overview: The Grenadier is an assault-weight Inner Sphere battlesuit developed by the Hahm-Heinze Design Bureau for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. Designed to mount the heaviest weapon systems possible on a single suit frame, the Grenadier prioritized raw firepower over mobility or protection. The suit carries a fixed missile launcher, a modular weapon mount accommodating a range of battlefield roles, and an anti-personnel station for close-range defense. Standard stealth armor provides electronic signature reduction, though total protection is modest for the weight class. At two thousand kilograms, the Grenadier is too heavy for OmniMech transport, restricting deployment to ground-based insertion methods.
fluff.capabilities: This configuration integrates a battle armor C3 computer system with a heavy recoilless rifle and Firedrake support needler. The C3 network link allows troopers to share targeting data with other networked units, improving accuracy across the entire formation. The heavy recoilless rifle delivers greater kinetic energy than the standard light version, effective against medium armor at moderate range. The Firedrake needler handles anti-personnel duties at close quarters. As a networked fire support platform, the configuration's value scales with the size and coordination of the C3 network it operates within. In isolation, the suit loses the network's accuracy bonuses and functions as a competent but unremarkable ballistic combatant. The absence of a missile system reduces anti-armor punch compared to other Hunter-Killer variants.
fluff.deployment: Augmented five-trooper C3 Hunter-Killer squads maximize the network's force multiplication effect by adding another data node to the formation. The Federated Suns Armored Cavalry adopted the five-suit configuration for its reconnaissance battle armor platoons, where the C3 link fed targeting data back to following armored formations in real time. The additional trooper also provides security for the squad during the vulnerable moments when operators focus on network coordination rather than local threats.
fluff.history:
The Hahm-Heinze Design Bureau began developing what would become the Grenadier when NAIS first started producing battle armor for the Federated Commonwealth. Drawing on long-standing ties to General Motors' plants on Talcott and Salem, the firm had access to early prototypes that informed their work. Nearly a decade of development produced a concept focused on mounting the heaviest possible weapon systems on a single suit. Hahm-Heinze approached the AFFC in 3062 with the finished design and two prototypes, but the FedCom Civil War consumed resources and attention, and the Federated Commonwealth initially passed on the Grenadier.

Only after the conflict demonstrated the suit's battlefield potential did production begin in earnest, with General Motors on Talcott and Albion Advanced Technologies on New Avalon manufacturing the design. Sales remained steady but slow through the Jihad years, hampered by disrupted supply lines and transportation. GM responded with an aggressive public relations effort called "Operation Parade," recruiting retired armored infantrymen to demonstrate the suit's effectiveness in field exercises and actual combat deployments alongside AFFS commands. The campaign proved successful enough that GM began offering alternative weapon configurations based on accumulated field reports and combat data.
fluff.manufacturer: Albion Advanced Technologies and Products|General Motors
